images.title: Levelling the guava stacks
images.purpose: Show five unequal stacks of guavas and the level at 6 they all reach when guavas move from tall stacks to short ones.
images.composition: Five stacks of round guavas in a row in the centre, crossed by one dashed level line, with the calculation in the upper right and white space around.
exact_structure: Exactly 5 vertical stacks of round guavas on a grey (#6B7280) baseline, from left to right holding 3, 8, 10, 5 and 4 guavas (30 in total); each count written under its stack.
One reddish purple (#CC79A7) dashed horizontal line across all stacks at the height of 6 guavas.
Guavas at or below the line are filled green (#009E73): 3, 6, 6, 5 and 4 in the five stacks.
Guavas above the line are filled amber (#E69F00), showing they will move: 2 on the stack of 8 and 4 on the stack of 10, so 6 amber guavas in all.
Empty grey dashed circles fill the gaps up to the line on the short stacks: 3 on the stack of 3, 1 on the stack of 5 and 2 on the stack of 4, so 6 empty circles in all, equal to the 6 amber guavas.
Label at the right end of the line: Fair share: 6 each. In the upper right: 30 ÷ 5 = 6.
rejection: the total number of drawn guavas different from 30
the number of amber guavas different from the number of empty circles (6 each)
the level line drawn at any height other than 6
faces or figures added to the scene
images.takeaway: The fair share is the level reached when the total is shared equally, and it equals the mean.
images.description: Five stacks of 3, 8, 10, 5 and 4 guavas with a purple dashed line at 6: the six amber guavas above the line fill the six empty dashed spaces below it.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which guavas move and where they go, then check that the level 6 is 30 ÷ 5; repeat in words for Parag's group of 6.

image_decisions.why: Guava stacks with a level line show the mean as a fair share.
